Spy Photos: 2027 Hyundai Porter LT2 Caught With Less Camo, Features Pleos Connect
20 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The next-generation Porter looks different from the cab-over truck we've known for more than two decades now. The latest spy photos of the 2027 model show a longer and more angular front end, complete with rectangular headlights near the outer edges. Replacing the almost vertical front profile of the Porter II, a stepped nose is on the menu as well.
LT2 is what Hyundai calls the newcomer internally, and the latest prototype is rocking a fairly small cabin that leaves plenty of room for the bed. The flatbed test vehicle is most interesting when admired from either side, for its design creates a more pronounced separation between the passenger cell and the front of the vehicle than its predecessor.
From the standpoint of styling, the simple headlight clusters flank a mostly closed panel. Whether that means the pictured vehicle is electric or not, we can't tell for certain from these photos. A more camouflaged prototype from October 2026, however, confirmed that electric muscle is coming to the Porter. Look even closer, and you will notice flatter and more angular surfacing than before.
The safety cell is mostly flat on three sides, flaunting a dramatic windshield rake for good measure. Pictured on good ol' steelies, the work-spec prototype integrates a low-height flat cargo bed with three hinged side and rear gates. Tie-down points are visible as well, and the same can be said about its rectangular taillights.
White-painted bars prevent rear window damage, as you'd expect from this kind of commercial vehicle. Regarding the reason why the LT2 looks so differently from the outgoing model, the flat-front design is gone to meet stricter frontal crash safety regs.
Moving the cabin backward behind the front wheels and adopting a semi-hood layout results in more front structure, including crumple zones, between the front bumper and the driver's legs.
Photo: SH Proshots The LT2 is expected to be sold in Europe as well, hence the safety-conscious design. A very popular truck in South Korea, the current Porter is especially popular with delivery companies and construction business. With the LT2, both electric and liquefied petroleum gas powertrains are planned. Hearsay suggests that no diesel or gasoline options are planned.
Spied last month, the more camouflaged electric prototype showed a visible charging connection and a black-painted frame with a marking that indicates four-wheel drive . In other words, the electric LT2 should offer at least one dual-motor option when it goes live in the first half of 2027.
Based on the only interior pic snapped by our carparazzo, the LT2 is also getting Pleos Connect software. You can think of Pleos Connect as the key to Hyundai's software-defined vehicle strategy. Pleos combines infotainment, cloud connectivity, vehicle control functions, and fleet management capabilities. In the world of commercial vehicles, Pleos could be incredibly useful.
Consider a delivery business that operates a bunch of LT2s. Fleet management software would help an operator monitor the fleet's condition, check maintenance schedules, coordinate servicing effortlessly, and so forth, making everyone's job easier. The wider Pleos ecosystem supports advanced ADAS, with Hyundai planning a Level 2+ rollout in the latter part of 2027.
